text:
ConocoPhillips fell 3.6% today to $134.40, following a sharp three-day decline from $142.28 on November 13th. The move coincides with oil prices dropping—US crude fell to $89.53 per barrel today from higher levels earlier this month—suggesting broad energy sector weakness. While Middle East tensions (Iran attacks, Strait of Hormuz concerns) have been in the news, oil prices themselves have retreated, which is the more direct pressure on an oil producer's near-term stock price.

The decline also fits a wider pattern: energy stocks face headwinds from long-term demand uncertainty, even as geopolitical risks flash across headlines. The IEA warning about data center power demand doubling by 2030 hints at competition for investment dollars and energy resources shifting away from traditional oil companies toward power infrastructure plays, though this is a slower-moving structural story than today's price drop.
